review_notes: I reviewed the whole file, lines 1–231. I did not open the related Coding files, so I did not search them for existing sum-transport lemmas. The only places with similar proof steps are the two mem-characterisation proofs, `parityExtension_punctureAt` and `parityExtension_reindex`. Both transport a coordinate sum along an equivalence with `Equiv.sum_comp`, then rewrite with a pointwise hypothesis `hyx`. In the backward directions this is a two- or three-line calculation: `rw [← Equiv.sum_comp ...] at hsum; simp only [hyx] at hsum` in one proof, and `rw [← Equiv.sum_comp ...] at hys; simpa only [hyx] using hys` in the other. A shared helper would be a thin wrapper around `Equiv.sum_comp`, which the rubric rules out as insufficient. In the forward directions the arguments differ. `parityExtension_punctureAt` shows that two zero-sum words agreeing on `some` are equal, by applying `parityExtend_comp_some` twice. `parityExtension_reindex` instead derives the value at `none` from the sums of the transported coordinates. These have little shared reasoning, and extracting a lemma from either would save only a few lines. The earlier lemmas (injectivity, `mem_parityExtension`, the map/equiv lemmas) are short, and each uses different API. Nothing here meets the bar of nontrivial repeated proof machinery.
